wave: CORRECTNESS -- a single non-UTF-8 .adl/.md/repo.toml file aborted the entire pipeline instead of being lossily read like every other artifact-read call site
wave_title: `runtime::census::extraction::extract_semantics` already establishes, in its own doc comment, the correct discipline for a per-artifact file-read failure: 'Never `?`-propagate: one artifact's read failure must not abort extraction of every artifact that comes after it in `inventory.artifacts`' -- and follows it, via an explicit `match fs::read_to_string(...) { Ok(..) => ..., Err(read_error) => { record a DiagnosticCode::InvalidInput ... } }`. Three other file-reading call sites in `adapter/src/lib.rs` did not follow that already-established discipline: `visit_adl_sources` (`.atlas/declared/*.adl`), `audit_repository` (`.atlas/repo.toml`), and `visit_docs` (`.atlas/**/*.md`) each called `fs::read_to_string(path)?` unconditionally. `fs::read_to_string` returns `Err(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData)` for any file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 -- a single corrupted or hostile-encoded `.adl`/`.md`/`repo.toml` file therefore aborted `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`docs audit`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare` entirely, producing no report at all, regardless of how many other well-formed files existed alongside it.

generation_model.G_n: 5c5a23404f (fix(cli): every subcommand's io::Error now names the offending --root path) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct grep sweep of production (non-test) code for `todo!`/`unimplemented!`/`FIXME` (found nothing actionable -- one false-positive match inside a test fixture string) and for `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` in the Cargo-lockfile and ADL parsers (both clean -- zero panics in production code, only in `#[cfg(test)]` modules; `Vec::windows(3)` indexing and slice-pattern-guarded indexing in the ADL parser confirmed safe by construction). Pivoted to auditing every `fs::read_to_string` call site across `adapter`/`core`/`runtime` for the crash class the two immediately preceding generations (bf2833e2, 5c5a23404f) had just fixed for `.atlas`-directory-absence and CLI-root-absence. Found that `runtime::census::extraction::extract_semantics` (the one call site that processes ordinary source files) already has the correct discipline, explicitly documented in its own comment -- and that three sibling call sites in `adapter/src/lib.rs` do not. Falsified directly: constructed a real scratch repository with one well-formed `.adl` file and one file containing a lone invalid UTF-8 byte sequence; `systemize` aborted with exit 2 and zero JSON output, confirmed via the real rebuilt binary before writing any fix.

priority_classification: correctness / hostile-input handling (priority 1/2) -- the third instance this session of the same underlying defect class (an io::Error from a single artifact's read aborting the whole pipeline instead of producing a typed report), now fixed at its remaining three call sites in one coherent change, closing the class rather than leaving two more crash paths for a future generation to rediscover one at a time.

design_decisions.question: Extend `AdlDiagnostic`/`DocsReport`/`RepoAudit` with an explicit 'this file was not valid UTF-8' fact (matching extraction.rs's explicit `DiagnosticCode::InvalidInput`), or lossy-decode and let the existing diagnostic machinery react naturally?
design_decisions.decision: Lossy-decode with `String::from_utf8_lossy` (the same technique `Path::to_string_lossy` already uses elsewhere in this codebase for exactly this kind of display-safety tradeoff). Extraction.rs's richer per-artifact diagnostic channel exists because semantic extraction already carries a `Vec<ExtractionDiagnostic>` per batch with no other natural place to record 'this file could not be analyzed'; `AdlSource`/the docs walker/the manifest reader have no equivalent per-file diagnostic channel today, and building one (extending `AdlSource`'s shape, threading a new error channel through `compile_adl`/`DocsReport`/`RepoAudit` and every one of their callers) is a materially larger, higher-risk change for the same observable benefit given the 12-consecutive-generation session's own emphasis on minimal, precisely-scoped fixes. `from_utf8_lossy` still satisfies every real requirement: the file is never silently dropped (still counted, still present in `sources`/`documents_total`), its valid content survives byte-for-byte, and only the genuinely undecodable bytes become a visible U+FFFD that naturally trips the *existing* diagnostic machinery (confirmed end-to-end: the corrupted line surfaced as a real `ATLAS-E010` 'unrecognized ADL declaration' diagnostic quoting the replacement character verbatim, rather than a generic or missing signal).

design_decisions.question: Fix only the one call site the falsification scenario targeted (`visit_adl_sources`), or all three?
design_decisions.decision: All three in one coherent change. `audit_repository`'s manifest read and `visit_docs`'s per-document read are the exact same defect (an unconditional `fs::read_to_string(...)?` on untrusted file content), discovered by the same audit pass, and `audit_repository`'s manifest read in particular runs even earlier in the real pipeline (`systemize` calls it immediately after `snapshot_git`) -- leaving it unfixed would mean a non-UTF-8 `repo.toml` still aborts every real entry point with zero report, an equally severe instance of the same class this generation set out to close.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A repository containing one file with invalid UTF-8 bytes -- in `.atlas/declared/*.adl`, `.atlas/repo.toml`, or any `.atlas/**/*.md` doc -- no longer aborts `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`docs audit`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare`. The file's valid content is preserved byte-for-byte, undecodable byte sequences become the standard U+FFFD replacement character, and the malformed file still participates in every downstream account (still present in `sources`, still counted in `documents_total`, still distinguished from a genuinely-missing manifest) -- it is never silently dropped, and its corruption remains visible through the diagnostics the existing parsers already produce for unrecognized syntax.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Three new falsification-first regression tests in `adapter/src/lib.rs`: `a_non_utf8_adl_file_does_not_abort_reading_the_rest_of_the_declared_tree`, `a_non_utf8_repo_manifest_does_not_abort_the_repository_audit`, `a_non_utf8_doc_does_not_abort_auditing_the_rest_of_the_tree`. Each constructs a real scratch directory with a genuinely invalid-UTF-8 file (confirmed to reproduce the exact claimed crash against the unfixed code for the `.adl` case before any fix was written) and a well-formed sibling, then asserts both files are accounted for and the well-formed sibling's content survives intact.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Real, rebuilt `atlas-systemizer` binary invoked against the original scratch repository that first surfaced the bug (one well-formed `.adl` file plus one containing raw `0xFF 0xFE` bytes): previously exit 2 with zero JSON output; now exit 0 with a full typed report, `coding_admission.allowed: false` (correctly -- the corrupted declaration is real syntax garbage and rightly fails ADL parsing), and an `ATLAS-E010` diagnostic quoting the corrupted line verbatim including the visible replacement character. Full workspace re-run (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`) and a fresh `systemize` run against the real Atlas-Studio repository itself confirm zero regression to any existing gate, blocker, or test.

implementation.adapter/src/lib.rs: `visit_adl_sources`, `audit_repository`, and `visit_docs` each changed from `fs::read_to_string(path)?` to `String::from_utf8_lossy(&fs::read(&path)?).into_owned()`. Three new falsification-first regression tests.

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. A single file with invalid UTF-8 bytes anywhere Atlas reads repository content directly (.atlas/declared/*.adl, .atlas/repo.toml, .atlas/**/*.md) previously aborted the entire pipeline with zero report, regardless of how many other well-formed files existed alongside it -- the same defect class fixed for the missing-.atlas-directory and missing-CLI-root cases in the two immediately preceding generations, now closed at its three remaining call sites. Every malformed file is now lossily decoded, never dropped, and its corruption remains visible through the diagnostics the existing parsers already produce, verified with three falsification-first regression tests and a real rebuilt-binary run, with zero regression to the real repository's own state or any existing test.
